domain: Chemical and nuclear-thermal propulsion, fluids and combustion

bottlenecks.name: Turbulence and turbulent-combustion modeling (closure error and CFD cost)
bottlenecks.description: Wall heat flux for regenerative cooling, propellant mixing, nozzle separation and injector flow all ride on turbulence closures. RANS cannot reliably predict separated flows (CFD Vision 2030 reviews); ML closures often fail to generalize (JFM 2025; arXiv 2604.25824). LES at engine conditions is prohibitively expensive (JAXA 2025), and stiff chemistry dominates reacting-flow cost: one LES realization of 2 ms of a spray with a 54-species mechanism took 48,000 core-hours and up to 20 days (UConn 2023). Exascale runs reach 60 billion cells (Pele on Frontier) and still cannot do engine-scale DNS.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Mixed. Genuinely open: closures that generalize and a convergence theory for LES (prop-closure-theory, prop-les-convergence-theory). Solved in principle but scarce experts or labor: certified reduced chemistry, solution verification and UQ (prop-stiff-chemistry, prop-cfd-auto-vv), where on-demand AI is the unlock. Navier–Stokes regularity is irrelevant here (P5, nil). For the open part, data binds, not cognition.

bottlenecks.name: Combustion dynamics: thermoacoustic instability, ignition and relight, detonation-engine wave modes
bottlenecks.description: Instability is still found and fixed on the test stand. The F-1's 'Project Go' ran 2,000 tests on 210 injector designs (enginehistory.org). Network models now predict acoustic frequencies within <5% (de Jong Cantarino et al. 2026), but growth rates and triggering depend on flame response at 100-350 bar, which is not predictable. In 2026 Starship showed live transient problems: Raptor 3 shutdowns <20 s into boostback (Flight 12) and only 10 of 13 booster engines relighting on Flight 13 (Jul 25, 2026). RDRE wave-mode bifurcation and injector coupling are open research while NASA hardware runs 340-s firings.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Stability certificates and bifurcation analysis of reduced models are expert-scarce applied math, the clearest P1 win (prop-certified-stability-rom: High by 2031 in S2). Flame response and RDE mode theory are open physics problems that need experiments (Medium in S2).

bottlenecks.name: Cryogenic fluid management in microgravity (boil-off, self-pressurization, slosh, chilldown, transfer, gauging)
bottlenecks.description: The critical path for Starship HLS: NASA OIG (Mar 2026) calls cryogenic transfer 'one of the most significant technical challenges'; tanker estimates range from SpaceX's '10-ish' to NASA's 'high teens'. Even in 1 g, NASA's validated CFD ranges from within 3% (laminar) to 15-16% under-prediction of tank pressure and up to 40% error on vapor temperature (k-omega SST), hinging on a tuned evaporation coefficient (Kartuzova et al., SciTech 2025). Microgravity flight data are scarce.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Mostly data-limited. Once Starship transfer and LOXSAT flight data exist, calibration and uncertainty analysis are routine applied math. Gauging has a genuine inverse-problem component; family 365 (T3) marks a nonuniqueness ceiling.

bottlenecks.name: Engine life, thermomechanical fatigue and reuse
bottlenecks.description: Reuse economics turn on refurbishment intervals. Life prediction is limited by heat-flux uncertainty, plasticity-model choice and lack of specimen data (Lisbon thesis 2024; Polito 2025), with additively-manufactured parts adding scatter. Methods (Morrow, Norton, Miner) rest on SSME-era data.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Strong. Probabilistic life modeling with UQ is expert-scarce, solved-in-principle applied math (prop-life-twin). Operators already hold fleet data. The heat-flux input inherits the closure problem.

bottlenecks.name: Turbomachinery: cavitation instabilities, rotordynamics, start transients
bottlenecks.description: Rotating cavitation, cavitation surge and rotordynamic instability drive turbopump failures. CFD predictions depend strongly on the cavitation and turbulence model chosen; 3D linear perturbation theories with dynamic transfer matrices are advancing (Pisa thesis 2025). Start and relight sequences are stiff transient systems with uncertain two-phase chilldown physics.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Stability of transfer-matrix and rotordynamic models is applied math that S2 makes cheap; the cavitation-compliance inputs need rigs and closures.

bottlenecks.name: Verification, validation and credibility of simulation
bottlenecks.description: Code verification, solution verification, UQ and credibility assessment (NASA-STD-7009 style) are known methods that are rarely done in full on engine CFD because they are labor-intensive (general). This is why tests are often run to settle questions a simulation may already have answered.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: The biggest solved-in-principle-but-expensive category: automated V&V (prop-cfd-auto-vv, P1->P2) and formally verified controller software (prop-verified-engine-software, P2). Certification acceptance gates the credit.

bottlenecks.name: Nuclear thermal propulsion: fuel and materials in hot hydrogen, test infrastructure, policy
bottlenecks.description: Core materials must survive 2,500-3,000 K hydrogen at >3 MPa under irradiation; GA-EMS fuel survived six cycles to 2,600 K (Jan 2025). Neutron transport is mature (general). DRACO was cancelled in 2025 on ROI grounds tied to falling launch costs (Breaking Defense, Jun 27, 2025); Congress put >=$110M into NTP for FY2026, but the April 2026 Space Nuclear Initiative prioritizes NEP (SR-1 Freedom, Mars 2028) and surface power. A ground test needs an exhaust-capture facility (designs exist, NASA 2023).
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Little. The binding gates are irradiation testing, facilities, approvals and money. Catalog links (278, 275, T1) only restate known limits of DFT.

nodes.title: Forced Navier–Stokes blowup independently checked
nodes.description: Outside experts run Comparator on the Lean proof and audit the statement of OpenAI's Sep 8, 2026 claim that the forced 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes equations can blow up from smooth, finite-energy data, along with the concurrent Buckmaster–Alpöge Euler, Boussinesq and porous-medium blowup proofs. This moves the claim from T3 to T4.
nodes.status_oct2026: Claimed Sep 8, 2026 with a 166-page manuscript and Lean repository (~17 h formalization; ~88 h of ~10,000 agents). Buckmaster and Alpöge posted Lean-verified Euler/Boussinesq/IPM blowup preprints on Sep 7, followed by a public credit dispute. No independent review found as of Oct 7, 2026: T3. Duraiswami (arXiv 2609.17642, Sep 15, 2026) found nothing to suggest the mechanism is reachable in a flow one computes or builds. Related family 376 (universal computation in forced NS) is T1.
nodes.why: The Lean code is public and the dispute guarantees scrutiny, so a Comparator run plus a statement audit is likely within about 12 months in every scenario. The engineering consequence is a confidence change only (position d): the forced equations alone can fail to determine the flow, which CFD practice already assumes by adding numerical or model dissipation. No solver, closure or engine design changes.
nodes.strongest_case_small: The forcing is engineered to drive the singularity, and real propellants would cavitate or form shocks long before it occurs (Duraiswami 2026). Rocket CFD resolves or models scales where the continuum assumption itself fails. The propulsion impact is essentially nil. The node is on the tree to mark a dead end readers would otherwise take for a breakthrough.
nodes.signpost: First published Comparator report and statement audit for the NS Lean repository (via Hexagon or the IAS advisory group), expected within 6-12 months. A gap would drop the claim to T1.

nodes.title: Unforced Navier–Stokes (Clay problem) settled
nodes.description: AI resolves the actual Clay Millennium statement for the unforced 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes equations: global smoothness or blowup on R^3 or the torus.
nodes.status_oct2026: Open. Forced blowup is claimed (T3), as is Euler blowup (Buckmaster–Alpöge, Lean). Family 376 (T1) shows that forced flows can embed universal computation, the route Tao proposed toward blowup constructions.
nodes.why: Under S2, solvable depth doubles every 6-9 months, and the two hardest precursor steps (Euler blowup, forced NS blowup) fell in 2026, so removing the forcing by about 2029 is plausible. Either answer acts through P5 only. A blowup would occur at scales below the molecular mean free path in any real gas or liquid; a regularity proof would confirm what every code already assumes.
nodes.strongest_case_small: No propulsion code, closure or test plan depends on the answer: a $1M prize result with roughly zero engineering effect. Its effect on public perception ('AI solved fluid dynamics') may exceed its technical effect, a communications risk the paper should address directly.
nodes.signpost: A lab announces unforced NS blowup or regularity with a Lean proof, and the Clay Institute responds.

nodes.title: Convergence theory for turbulent simulations
nodes.description: A proven framework (for example statistical or measure-valued solutions) that states which LES/DNS statistics converge under mesh refinement, with computable error bounds, so that 'grid-converged LES' has a defined meaning.
nodes.status_oct2026: Open. LES has no classical grid-convergence theory; practitioners use heuristics such as resolving ~80% of turbulent kinetic energy (general). The Euler and forced-NS blowup claims (T3) reinforce that pointwise convergence can fail, so convergence has to be statistical.
nodes.why: This feeds prop-cfd-auto-vv: the credibility statement for an injector LES could carry a numerical error bar instead of an expert's judgment. If the bounds are computable, they would also show analysts when they are over-resolving, plausibly saving 2-4x compute on design LES (judgment, general).
nodes.strongest_case_small: The theory may give only asymptotic rates with no usable constants. Validation against experiment would still dominate credibility, and model-form (closure) error usually exceeds numerical error.
nodes.signpost: An AI-assisted proof of convergence rates for statistics of 3D LES with explicit constants, cited in an AIAA CFD workshop guideline.

nodes.title: Certified combustion-stability models
nodes.description: Low-order acoustic-network or Galerkin models of chamber thermoacoustics, delivered with rigorous linear and nonlinear stability margins: Lyapunov or sum-of-squares certificates and bounds on Hopf bifurcation and triggering amplitude under an uncertain flame-response band.
nodes.status_oct2026: Solved in principle but expert-scarce. DLR/TU Delft network models predict acoustic frequencies within <5% on two research combustors (de Jong Cantarino et al., IJSCD 2026). Growth rates and triggering thresholds still hinge on flame response, and reliable, efficient instability prediction remains rare (JAXA 2025). Family 143 [L] (uniform limit-cycle bounds, Hilbert's 16th) is T3 but theory only: it bounds how many oscillation states can coexist in planar polynomial amplitude models, with no practical constant.
nodes.why: Stability analysis of a given model is bespoke but routine mathematics, exactly the kind that becomes on-demand under position (a). With public research-grade models in 2027 (S2), a team can get certified margins for every injector variant in days instead of a specialist's months. The value is capped by the flame-response input (prop-flame-response).
nodes.strongest_case_small: Certifying the stability of a model with the wrong flame response gives false comfort: a proof of the wrong property. Bomb tests stay mandatory. The F-1 lesson is that triggered (nonlinear) instability is what destroys engines, and its inputs are physical.
nodes.signpost: A published AI-produced stability analysis that predicts unstable modes and triggering thresholds on a rig (DLR BKD/BKH, Purdue CVRC) before the test.

nodes.title: Fast chemistry with certified error
nodes.description: Reduced kinetic mechanisms and structure-preserving stiff integrators with provable error bounds on ignition delay, heat release and key species, so that detailed LOX/CH4 and LOX/H2 chemistry fits inside engine LES at a fraction of today's cost.
nodes.status_oct2026: Chemistry integration dominates reacting-flow cost: 48,000 core-hours for 2 ms of one spray LES with 54 species (UConn 2023). Mechanism reduction (DRG, QSS) is heuristic and checked by sampling. Family 149 (permanence for weakly reversible reaction networks, T1) gives a qualitative persistence guarantee for isothermal mass-action systems only. Conditional, theory only.
nodes.premise_tier: n/a (capability); 149 is T1, conditional and marginal
nodes.why: A 3-10x cut in reacting-LES cost (estimate, general) means 3-10x more design points per week and makes flame-response prediction affordable. Error certificates let teams trust reduced mechanisms outside their training conditions.
nodes.strongest_case_small: GPU chemistry and ML surrogates already deliver much of the speedup without proofs, and practitioners may not value certificates. Family 149 assumes isothermal, closed mass-action networks, while combustion is non-isothermal and open.
nodes.signpost: A reduced-mechanism generator with certified error bounds released in Cantera, Pele or a commercial CFD code.

nodes.title: Automated CFD verification and credibility
nodes.description: AI agents run code verification (manufactured solutions), solution verification (adjoint or a-posteriori error estimates), uncertainty quantification and NASA-STD-7009-style credibility assessment on every propulsion simulation at near-zero marginal cost.
nodes.status_oct2026: Solved in principle, but rarely done in full on engine-design CFD because it is labor-intensive (general). CFD Vision 2030 progress reviews flag separated-flow prediction and UQ as persistent gaps (Aerospace America, Dec 2022).
nodes.why: Every CFD result becomes a number with an error bar that separates numerical error from model-form error. That ends two expensive failure modes: hardware built on an unconverged simulation, and tests run to settle a question the simulation had already answered. It is also a prerequisite for any regulator credit for simulation.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Validation data, not verification labor, limit V&V. Error bars on RANS are dominated by closure error, which verification cannot remove.
nodes.signpost: An AI-generated credibility assessment accepted in a NASA or prime-contractor design review, or AI-automated solution verification in AIAA CFD Prediction Workshop entries.

nodes.title: Low-gravity propellant gauging limits
nodes.description: Proofs of which tank-fill states can be identified in microgravity from boundary sensors (capacitance, radio-frequency or impedance-type tomography), plus gauging algorithms with guaranteed error bounds.
nodes.status_oct2026: Gauging is a focus area of NASA's CFM portfolio, alongside boil-off and transfer. Family 365 [L] (joint metric and connection recovery from one boundary patch, with conductivity nonuniqueness) is T3 and acts as a ceiling: some interior configurations cannot be told apart from boundary data alone without priors or extra sensing.
nodes.why: Gauging uncertainty turns into reserve propellant: on a depot holding over 1,000 t, each 1% of gauging error is ~10 t of margin (illustrative, general). The ceiling side (P3) tells designers to stop pursuing tomography-only gauging and to fuse sensors with thermodynamic models.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Operators can gauge after a settling burn with conventional sensors and accept the margin. The nonuniqueness in family 365 concerns specific (often anisotropic) settings that may not match real tanks.
nodes.signpost: Flight gauging accuracy reported from LOXSAT or the Starship transfer demo (target <=1%).

nodes.title: Turbulence and combustion closures with guarantees
nodes.description: AI-built RANS, LES subgrid and flamelet closures that are realizable, frame-invariant and consistent in known limits, carry generalization bounds, and are validated across separated, swirling and reacting benchmark classes without per-case tuning.
nodes.status_oct2026: Open; this is the field's central modeling problem. RANS cannot reliably predict separated flows (CFD Vision 2030). ML closures often fail to generalize beyond their training data (JFM 2025; arXiv 2604.25824, Apr 2026). A propulsion example: k-omega SST under-predicts LH2 tank self-pressurization by 15-16% and vapor temperature by up to 40%, versus 3% for laminar and 7% for IDDES (Kartuzova et al., SciTech 2025).
nodes.why: Closure error is the dominant model-form error in propulsion CFD: wall heat flux for cooling, mixing, nozzle separation. Under S2 the cognitive part (deriving constrained closures, proving consistency) is fast. What binds is high-fidelity data at engine conditions. DNS at engine Reynolds numbers is infeasible even at exascale (Pele's largest run: 60 billion cells), and high-pressure reacting validation experiments take years.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Turbulence closure has resisted 60 years of work and may be fundamentally underdetermined, because averaging loses information. A provably consistent closure need not beat a tuned one on a specific engine. LES and hybrid methods are already replacing RANS in design-critical areas.
nodes.signpost: An AI-derived closure tops the NASA Turbulence Modeling Resource separated-flow cases and a blind AIAA workshop case without retuning.

nodes.title: Predictive flame response at engine pressures
nodes.description: First-principles prediction of injector flame transfer functions and transcritical real-fluid mixing for LOX/CH4 and LOX/H2 at 100-350 bar. This is the missing input that decides whether a chamber mode grows.
nodes.status_oct2026: Measured on subscale rigs or extracted from costly LES; wall-modeled LES at engine conditions is described as prohibitively expensive (JAXA 2025). Raptor 3 has demonstrated 350 bar chamber pressure (newspaceeconomy, Apr 16, 2026), deep in the supercritical regime where injection models lack validation (general).
nodes.why: With flame response predicted, certified reduced models (prop-certified-stability-rom) predict growth rates, not just frequencies. Validation can start against decades of archived rig data, but it then needs about a year of blind rig tests. That experimental year binds in S2 and S3 alike.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Flame response depends on manufacturing detail (injector tolerances, additive-manufacturing roughness) and on transient states that models won't capture. Rigs remain necessary for every new injector family.
nodes.signpost: Blind prediction of an unstable mode's frequency and amplitude to within ~10% on a JANNAF, ESA or DLR combustor before the test.

nodes.title: Predictive theory of detonation-engine wave modes
nodes.description: A validated model of how many detonation waves an RDRE runs, when it switches modes, and how injectors couple to the waves, as functions of flow rate, mixture and back-pressure, so that engines can be designed to hold one stable mode.
nodes.status_oct2026: Open research: wave-mode bifurcation (APS DFD 2025), dynamic injector-response models (Mar 2025), and model equations that capture qualitative mode-locking (arXiv 2003.06655). Hardware is ahead of theory: NASA InRoDES fired a 10,000 lbf-class LOX/LCH4 thrust chamber for >340 s (Sep and Dec 2025).
nodes.why: RDRE gains of up to ~10% in thrust and specific impulse, or a 5x lower injection feed pressure (NASA NTRS 2024), appear only with stable, predictable modes. This is nonlinear-dynamics mathematics that S2 makes cheap, and the validating hot-fire campaigns take days to weeks.
nodes.strongest_case_small: RDRE development is advancing empirically (340-s firings, Venus flight). Theory may mostly explain what tests already found; the real gates are thermal management of a compact chamber and nozzle integration.
nodes.signpost: A published model that predicts mode transitions on a new RDRE geometry blind, confirmed by NASA or AFRL tests.

nodes.title: Validated microgravity cryogenic fluid models
nodes.description: Predictive models of self-pressurization, slosh, line chilldown and tank-to-tank transfer in low gravity, validated on flight data with quantified uncertainty (tank pressure within ~5%, boil-off within ~10%).
nodes.status_oct2026: In 1 g, CFD reaches 3% (laminar) to 7% (IDDES) on tank pressure, but results hinge on the turbulence model and a tuned evaporation accommodation coefficient (Kartuzova et al., SciTech 2025). Microgravity data are scarce (ZBOT on ISS). NASA's CFM portfolio lists maturing predictive models through flight-prediction comparisons as an objective. LOXSAT (Eta Space/Rocket Lab, a 9-month LOX demo) was set for no earlier than Jul 17, 2026; the sources found do not confirm whether it has flown.
nodes.why: Boil-off and transfer losses drive the tanker count (SpaceX '10-ish' vs NASA 'high teens'). In an illustrative depot model (tables), boil-off of 0.05-0.3%/day costs ~1 extra tanker at one tanker per 6 days, and 0.3-0.5%/day costs 3-5 extra at one per 12 days. Validated models let operators set margins from prediction instead of conservatism. In S2 the analysis is near-instant once flight data exist, but the data arrive on the launch clock (2027 onward).
nodes.strongest_case_small: SpaceX will learn empirically from its own flights and keep the data, and margins will follow measured performance whether or not a public model exists.
nodes.signpost: Publication of transferred mass, boil-off and chilldown losses from the first Starship ship-to-ship transfer, or NASA model-vs-flight comparisons from LOXSAT.

nodes.title: Predictive plume–surface interaction for landers
nodes.description: Validated models of how lander engine plumes erode regolith (rarefied-to-continuum gas flow, granular ejecta, cratering), used to set landing-site and engine-placement requirements.
nodes.status_oct2026: NASA reports that poorly constrained flight data inhibit accurate PSI prediction. Langley's vacuum-sphere PSI tests run through spring 2026, and MSFC PSI tools support HLS (NTRS 2023). Families 363 (Boltzmann nonuniqueness with exact local conservation) and 364 (Boltzmann derived from Newtonian gases, incl. fluctuations) are T1 and touch the kinetic theory beneath DSMC. Conditional; P5 confidence only.
nodes.why: Multi-meganewton Raptor-class landing plumes on unprepared regolith are a mission risk for Starship HLS, and predictive PSI decides whether landing pads or high-mounted thrusters are needed. Family 364 would firm up the Boltzmann foundations for DSMC in the rarefied plume; family 363 flags where kinetic solutions need a selection principle.
nodes.strongest_case_small: DSMC already works for the gas phase. The gaps are granular physics and lunar flight data, which no theorem supplies, and operators can engineer around PSI with pads, throttling or thruster placement.
nodes.signpost: Pre-landing PSI predictions matched by post-landing imagery from CLPS or Artemis landers.

nodes.title: Nuclear thermal fuel behavior model
nodes.description: A validated multiphysics model of carbide or CERMET fuel corrosion, cracking and fission-product release in 2,500-3,000 K hydrogen under irradiation and thermal cycling. These are the physics that set NTP temperature, Isp and life.
nodes.status_oct2026: GA-EMS fuel survived six thermal cycles to 2,600 K in flowing hydrogen at MSFC (Jan 2025). Core materials that endure 2,500-3,000 K hydrogen at >3 MPa remain the critical obstacle (general literature). Neutron transport (Monte Carlo) is mature (general). Families 278 (Kohn–Sham ensemble representability fails) and 275 (QMA-hardness of continuum Coulomb energy) are T1: ceilings on DFT-based materials modeling. Conditional, P3.
nodes.why: Fuel life and temperature set NTP's ~900 s Isp, against ~450 s for LOX/LH2 (general). A predictive model narrows the irradiation test matrix. But irradiation in test reactors (months to years to accumulate fluence) binds: autonomous labs speed up non-nuclear hot-hydrogen tests, not neutron dose.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Fuel qualification is inherently empirical and regulators will require data. Families 278 and 275 confirm DFT limits that practitioners already work around.
nodes.signpost: Release of a combined hot-hydrogen plus irradiation dataset (INL/MSFC) with blind model predictions.

nodes.title: Design out combustion instability before hot fire
nodes.description: An integrated workflow (predicted flame response, a certified reduced-order stability model and uncertainty quantification) that ranks injector and chamber designs by stability margin before hardware is built, used on a real engine program.
nodes.status_oct2026: Instability is still found and fixed on the test stand. For the F-1, 'Project Go' ran 2,000 tests on 210 injector designs over two years before bomb tests showed damping within 45 ms (enginehistory.org; NASA History, Jul 12, 2019). Modern programs iterate faster with cheap additive injectors, but the loop remains test-driven.
nodes.why: If even a third of instability redesign loops are avoided, a new engine saves months to a year and tens of hardware sets (judgment, general). The math (stability certificates) is fast under S2; flame-response validation and qualification testing are not.
nodes.strongest_case_small: For well-funded teams, SpaceX-style rapid iteration with cheap 3D-printed injectors already makes testing cheaper than prediction (600+ Raptors built by Apr 2026). Bomb tests and stability rating stay mandatory, so the tests saved are development tests, not qualification tests.
nodes.signpost: An engine program reports first-article stability qualification with no injector redesign and credits predictive tools.

nodes.title: AI-generated engines at scale
nodes.description: Computational engineering models generate complete additively-manufactured engines (geometry, regenerative cooling, injectors) in weeks. The node counts as achieved when a >=200 kN AI-generated engine completes a full-duration hot fire.
nodes.status_oct2026: LEAP 71's Noyron generated a 5 kN LOX/kerosene aerospike that worked on its first firing (Dec 18, 2024). The 200 kN LOX/CH4 XRA-2E5 was printed as one Inconel part in 289 h (Mar 2026), with a hot fire planned before 2027. The Exploration Company licensed Noyron (Mar 24, 2026). Venus Aerospace credits 'AI-enabled design software' for its RDRE (Mercury Fund, Jul 21, 2026).
nodes.why: Design labor collapses toward zero, so the loop period is set by print time (~2 weeks for a large part) and test-stand availability. Once cap-design-optimization arrives, AI math adds guarantees such as proven cooling-channel thermal margins, but the loop already exists without it.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Design labor was never the long pole for large engines; reliability growth and qualification are. Noyron-style tools encode engineering rules rather than frontier mathematics, so the openai/math release adds little here.
nodes.signpost: A full-duration XRA-2E5 hot fire, and the first orbital flight on an AI-generated main engine.

nodes.title: Predictive turbopump cavitation and stability
nodes.description: Models that predict rotating cavitation, cavitation surge and rotordynamic instability for new inducer and pump designs before water-flow and hot-fire tests.
nodes.status_oct2026: CFD predictions of cavitation instabilities depend strongly on the chosen cavitation and turbulence models, and 3D linear perturbation theories with dynamic transfer matrices are advancing (Pisa thesis, Jun 2025). Several Raptor 3 engines shut down <20 s into boostback on a mid-2026 flight; commentary pointed to combustion, turbopump or sensor-redline margins, with no official cause (Nerra Network, Jun 18, 2026).
nodes.why: Turbopump instabilities are a leading cause of engine failures (general). Stability analysis of transfer-matrix models is applied math that S2 makes cheap, but predicting the cavitation-compliance and mass-flow-gain inputs needs closures and rig data.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Water-flow rig tests are cheap compared with hot fire, and design rules are mature, so prediction may save little.
nodes.signpost: A blind prediction of rotating-cavitation onset for a new inducer, confirmed in a rig test.

nodes.title: Probabilistic engine life prediction for reuse
nodes.description: Physics-based life models for thermomechanical fatigue, low-cycle fatigue and creep in chambers, turbines and additively-manufactured parts, with uncertainty quantification, updated after each flight from sensors and inspection.
nodes.status_oct2026: Life estimation is hampered by heat-flux uncertainty, the choice of plasticity model and a lack of specimen characterization (Lisbon thesis 2024; Polito 2025). The methods are Morrow, Norton and Miner, validated on SSME-era data. Families 372 (global uniqueness in smooth isotropic elasticity) and 366 (planar Mumford–Shah crack regularity) are T1 links to inspection inverse problems. Conditional, P5.
nodes.why: Reuse economics turn on refurbishment intervals. Probabilistic life models with UQ are expert-scarce applied math, the category S2 makes cheap. Operators already hold fleet data from hundreds of reflown engines, so data binds less here than elsewhere.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Operators extend life through fleet-leader experience anyway, so any gain is internal and hard to observe. Heat-flux uncertainty (a closure problem) limits physics-based accuracy.
nodes.signpost: An operator or NASA discloses model-based (not fleet-leader-only) engine life limits, or NASA accepts probabilistic life analysis for crewed reuse.

nodes.title: Predictive engine start and relight transients
nodes.description: Validated system-level models of line chilldown, ignition, turbopump spin-up and combustion onset for in-flight relights after a coast, used to design start sequences with quantified margin.
nodes.status_oct2026: A live 2026 problem: on Flight 13 (Jul 25, 2026) only 10 of 13 booster engines relit for landing, and about five were running at splashdown (Spaceflight Now). Start transients are stiff differential-algebraic systems with uncertain two-phase chilldown physics (general).
nodes.why: Relight reliability gates booster catch, ship landing and, most critically, HLS lunar descent after days to weeks in orbit. Modeling stiff transients with certified numerics is applied math, and every flight supplies validation data.
nodes.strongest_case_small: SpaceX will probably fix relight empirically within a few flights, and models will follow the data rather than lead it.
nodes.signpost: Several consecutive Starship flights with full booster and ship relight success, especially after long coasts.

nodes.title: Formally verified engine control software
nodes.description: Machine-checked proofs that engine-controller and health-management logic (start sequencing, redlines, abort logic, numerical filters) meets its specification, produced by AI agents at low cost and accepted in certification.
nodes.status_oct2026: Certification standards already give credit for formal methods (DO-178C/DO-333), but AI agents and Lean are not qualified tools. The agentic formalization capability exists: openai/math formalized the main results of 162 papers in weeks. The 2026 Raptor 3 boostback shutdowns, with sensor trip as one hypothesis, show why redline logic matters.
nodes.why: Engine controllers are safety-critical, and false or missed shutdowns from redline logic recur as a failure mode (general). AI proofs cut verification cost and make full formal coverage practical. The band is capped at Medium because it needs certification acceptance.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Most engine failures are physical rather than software. Commercial launch licensing does not require formal verification, and writing correct specifications remains the bottleneck.
nodes.signpost: The first NASA crewed-program or FAA certification credit for AI-generated formal proofs of propulsion controller software.

nodes.title: Ship-to-ship cryogenic transfer demonstrated
nodes.description: Two Starships dock in low Earth orbit and transfer tens to 100+ tonnes of LOX and liquid methane, with measured boil-off, chilldown loss and transfer efficiency.
nodes.status_oct2026: Starship reached orbit for the first time on Flight 14 (Sep 28, 2026) and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites (Mach33, Sep 30, 2026). Ship-to-ship transfer has not flown yet and could come as soon as Flight 15 in late 2026 (Space.com). Internal tank-to-tank transfer was done on Mar 14, 2024. NASA OIG (Mar 2026) calls cryogenic transfer 'one of the most significant technical challenges'.
nodes.why: Flights and vehicle readiness set the timing, and AI mathematics moves this node by roughly zero. It is on the tree because its data unlock prop-cfm-models and, downstream, the refueling economy.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Not applicable: this node exists to show the physical clock. The AI-math effect on its date is nil.
nodes.signpost: Announcement and flight of the propellant-transfer mission, with the transferred mass disclosed.

nodes.title: Detonation engine flies in space
nodes.description: A rotating detonation rocket engine of about 1,000 lbf or more operates as primary propulsion in a space or lander flight demonstration, beyond suborbital hops.
nodes.status_oct2026: Venus Aerospace flew a 2,000 lbf RDRE to 4,400 ft (May 2025). Juno Propulsion won a NASA TechLeap prize for a NASA-funded flight test later in 2026 (small thruster). NASA's InRoDES is a 10,000 lbf-class pump-fed LOX/LCH4 engine with >340 s chamber firings in 2025; a vacuum test comes next, then transfer to industry.
nodes.why: Hardware is limited by testing and funding. Cheaper analysis under S2 (mode theory, thermal design) trims iterations but cannot shorten vacuum testing, flight integration or the wait for a funded flight slot. Autonomous test campaigns under S3 pull the date about a year earlier.
nodes.strongest_case_small: A small in-space RDRE firing (Juno) may come in 2026-27 regardless of AI math. The >=1,000 lbf demo depends on a customer and money, not mathematics.
nodes.signpost: A Juno Propulsion in-space RDRE firing, NASA InRoDES vacuum-test results, or a lander provider baselining an RDRE.

nodes.title: Nuclear thermal engine ground hot fire
nodes.description: A fission-heated hydrogen engine (5-12.5 klbf subscale) fired on the ground with full exhaust capture: the first U.S. NTP reactor test since NERVA (1972).
nodes.status_oct2026: DRACO was cancelled in the FY2026 budget request (May 2025) because falling launch costs eroded its ROI (DARPA's McHenry, Breaking Defense, Jun 27, 2025). Congress directed >=$110M for NTP in FY2026, and Administrator Isaacman committed to execute it (Sen. Britt, Apr 29, 2026). The White House Space Nuclear Initiative (Apr 14, 2026) prioritizes NEP (SR-1 Freedom, 20 kWe, Mars launch at end-2028) and lunar surface power, with 'common NEP/NTP components'. A high-pressure exhaust capture system for 5-12.5 klbf tests exists as a design (NASA, 2023).
nodes.why: As of Oct 2026 there is no funded NTP engine program of record. A reactor ground test needs a program start, a fueled reactor, an exhaust-capture facility and nuclear safety approval, which on historical precedent takes 5+ years from start (general). AI compresses design and safety-analysis documentation (S2/S3) but not facility construction, fuel fabrication or approvals.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Policy and money decide this node, and the policy pivot to NEP was driven by cost and launch prices, not mathematics.
nodes.signpost: FY2027 or FY2028 budgets fund an NTP ground-test facility and reactor, or DOE and NASA announce an NTP program of record.

nodes.title: Full lunar-lander refueling campaign
nodes.description: Roughly 10-20 tanker flights fill a depot in LEO, which transfers a full load to Starship HLS for a lunar landing (uncrewed demo or crewed).
nodes.status_oct2026: NASA OIG (Mar 2026): more than 10 tankers are needed, the landing is planned for 2028, and NASA tracks a 'top risk' that cryogenic technologies won't be mature. ASAP (Sep 2025) warned HLS could be 'years late'. Estimates run from SpaceX's '10-ish' to NASA's 'high teens'. NASA plans an interim Artemis test flight in LEO in 2027 before landing attempts (Spaceflight Now, Jul 2026).
nodes.why: Launch cadence binds. At one tanker every ~6 days a campaign takes about 2 months, and every slip in cadence multiplies boil-off losses (tables). Validated boil-off and transfer models (prop-cfm-models) and reliable relights (prop-start-transient) save ~1-4 tankers per mission and some schedule margin: months, not years. S3's broad AI acceleration of hardware iteration is what lifts the band to High.
nodes.strongest_case_small: AI mathematics is not on the critical path. Vehicle reliability, launch cadence, docking and pad turnaround are.
nodes.signpost: The first depot-filling campaign with >=5 tankers flown, and NASA confirming a landing date after the 2027 LEO test.

nodes.title: Detonation engines in operational service
nodes.description: RDREs used as production propulsion on a commercial lander, upper stage or in-space vehicle, with predictable, qualified behavior.
nodes.status_oct2026: There is no operational RDRE anywhere; only demonstrations exist (see prop-rde-flight-demo).
nodes.why: Operational use requires a qualified engine whose mode behavior is predictable across throttle and mixture ranges, and that predictability is what mode theory buys. Qualifying a new combustion mode for operational use has historically taken several years after the first flight demo (general).
nodes.strongest_case_small: Even with perfect theory, a ~10% Isp gain may not justify the qualification cost for most missions. Defense missiles and hypersonics, not space, may be the first operational users.
nodes.signpost: A lander or upper-stage provider contracting an RDRE as baseline propulsion.

nodes.title: Model-based engine reuse life
nodes.description: Reusable engines whose overhaul and inspection intervals are set by validated probabilistic life models, extending the flights between overhauls (for example 2x) without added risk.
nodes.status_oct2026: Reuse life today is extended mainly by fleet-leader experience (general). Raptor 3 had accumulated >40,000 s of runtime by Apr 2026 (newspaceeconomy).
nodes.why: Cheaper refurbishment and faster turnaround feed directly into launch cost, and a doubled overhaul interval is plausible once life models are calibrated on fleet data. The accumulation of fleet data, flight by flight, sets the pace.
nodes.strongest_case_small: The gains are internal and hard to observe, and operators may extend life empirically just as fast.
nodes.signpost: Operator statements tying engine overhaul intervals to analytic life models, or NASA reuse certification for crewed flights citing probabilistic life analysis.

nodes.title: Nuclear thermal stage for crewed Mars
nodes.description: A flight-qualified NTP stage (~900 s Isp) available for crewed Mars transits, cutting trip time by up to ~25% (per DOE) and reducing crew radiation dose.
nodes.status_oct2026: There is no funded NTP flight program (DRACO was cancelled in 2025), and NEP was chosen for SR-1 Freedom (2028).
nodes.why: This requires a ground test, a flight demo and crew-rating, each a multi-year effort, and none has started. Math is not on the critical path.
nodes.strongest_case_small: The node is on the tree to mark a ceiling: AI math cannot fund a reactor or license a test.
nodes.signpost: An NTP flight-demo program of record with a launch date.

nodes.title: Engine development time and cost cut
nodes.description: New liquid engines reach qualification with materially fewer hot-fire tests and redesign loops (for example >=30% fewer than comparable heritage programs), with the saving attributed to predictive tools.
nodes.status_oct2026: Development remains test-driven. SpaceX has built 600+ Raptors through large-scale test-fail-fix iteration (newspaceeconomy, Apr 2026).
nodes.why: Design and analysis compress (P1), but reliability demonstration is statistical. Showing 0.99 reliability at 90% confidence with zero failures takes ~230 tests (n = ln 0.1 / ln 0.99) unless customers accept model-based Bayesian credit. Models cut redesign loops, not demonstration tests. Engine programs also run 3-7 years, so few programs started with S2 capability will qualify by 2031.
nodes.strongest_case_small: The cheapest route to reliability is already high-rate testing of cheap hardware, so prediction competes with a very fast empirical loop.
nodes.signpost: A program publicly attributing a reduced hot-fire count to predictive tools, or a customer (NASA, USSF) accepting model-based reliability credit.

nodes.title: Routine orbital refueling economy
nodes.description: Depots and tankers operate routinely, with dozens of cryogenic transfers per year supporting lunar landers, Mars ships and high-energy missions, and boil-off and transfer losses are predicted rather than padded.
nodes.status_oct2026: Not yet demonstrated. Eta Space targets a commercial LOX depot (Cryo-Dock) by 2030 (satnews, May 2026).
nodes.why: The economics depend on tankers per delivered tonne. Validated boil-off, transfer and gauging models are worth ~1-4 tankers per HLS-class mission (illustrative tables), or 10-30% of campaign launches. The rest comes down to cadence and vehicle reuse.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Launch cadence and vehicle cost dominate, so model-driven savings are second-order.
nodes.signpost: More than 20 ship-to-ship transfers in a calendar year, or a third-party depot (for example Cryo-Dock) receiving propellant.

scenario_contrast: The tree compresses from the top. S1 (Plateau): public research-grade math arrives ~2028, AI applied math ~2029-30, and AI physics theory after 2031. Tier-2 nodes (certified stability models, automated V&V, gauging limits, life prediction) land 2029-2030 at Medium. Tier-3 physics nodes (closures, flame response, plume–surface interaction, NTP fuels) mostly slip past 2031. Tier 5-6 nodes run on their physical clocks: transfer demo 2027, HLS refueling 2029, RDE in-space demo 2029. S2 (Exponential, base case): tier-2 nodes pull forward 1-2 years to 2027-2028 and reach High. Tier-3 physics nodes arrive 2028-2030 but stay Medium, because high-pressure reacting data, microgravity flight data and irradiation data bind once theory is cheap. Tier-4 tools land 2028-2030. Tier 5-6 nodes move 0-1 year, because launch cadence, test stands, qualification and appropriations bind, and tier-7 outcomes mostly land after 2031. S3 (Recursive): autonomous labs and AI-accelerated hardware iteration pull experiment-gated nodes a further ~1 year (flame response, RDE, NTP fuel model) and lift HLS refueling to High. Irradiation time, nuclear approvals, NTP capital and the statistics of reliability demonstration (~230 zero-failure tests for 0.99 at 90% confidence) do not compress. Between S1 and S2, the median cognitive node (tiers 1-3) moves ~2 years earlier and the median physical node (tiers 5-6) about 0 years. Shared upstream years assumed here: cap-research-math-public S1 2028 / S2 2027 / S3 2027; cap-applied-math 2029 / 2027 / 2027; cap-physics-theory >2031 / 2028 / 2028; cap-design-optimization 2030 / 2028 / 2028; cap-autonomous-labs >2031 / 2029 / 2028; infra-verified-numerics 2030 / 2028 / 2028; infra-tool-qualification >2031 / 2030 / 2029; verif-independent-check 2027 in all three.
key_insights: Propulsion is bound by physical clocks. Under the exponential base case (S2), cognitive nodes (tiers 1-3) arrive ~2 years earlier than under the plateau, while flight and mission nodes (tiers 5-6) move by 0-1 year, because launch cadence, test stands, qualification, irradiation time and appropriations bind.

Navier–Stokes is a dead end for propulsion engineering. The Sep 8, 2026 forced-blowup claim (T3, unreviewed) and even a future resolution of the unforced Clay problem change confidence in the equations, not codes, closures or engines. An independent analysis (arXiv 2609.17642) finds the mechanism unreachable in buildable flows. The paper should say this plainly, because readers will assume the opposite.

The largest near-term gains are in expert-scarce work that is solved in principle: certified combustion-stability margins for reduced models, automated CFD verification and UQ, probabilistic engine-life prediction and gauging analysis. All travel P1, and all are High by 2031 under S2. The catalog contributes little here; the capability does (position a).

Where the physics is genuinely open (turbulence and combustion closures, flame response at 100-350 bar, microgravity cryogenics, plume–surface interaction), cheap theory meets a data wall. Under S2 the binding gate shifts from cognition to data, and the most valuable assets become data generators: Starship transfer flights, LOXSAT, high-pressure combustion rigs and vacuum-chamber plume tests.

Better boil-off models are worth more the slower the launch cadence. In an illustrative 1,200 t depot fill with 120 t tankers, boil-off of 0.05-0.3%/day costs ~1 extra tanker at one launch per 6 days but 3-5 extra at one per 12 days with 0.3-0.5%/day. Validated cryogenic models are worth ~1-4 tankers per HLS-class mission, roughly 10-30% of campaign launches.

Models cut redesign loops, not reliability demonstration. Showing 0.99 reliability at 90% confidence still takes ~230 zero-failure tests unless customers accept model-based Bayesian credit, so engine-development compression by 2031 is Low even in S2. The lever is a rule change, not a theorem.

Nuclear thermal propulsion is gated by policy and capital, not mathematics. DRACO died on ROI as launch costs fell; FY2026 holds only ~$110M; the April 2026 initiative prioritizes NEP. An NTP ground test by 2031 is Low and a crewed Mars NTP stage is Speculative in every scenario.

Catalog links to this domain are thin and mostly conditional. Families 376, 149, 363, 364, 278, 275, 372 and 366 are T1. Only 143 (limit cycles) and 365 (boundary-data nonuniqueness for gauging) are T3, and both are marginal: one bounds oscillation states with no practical constant, the other marks a ceiling on tomographic gauging.
nil_effects: Navier–Stokes regularity, forced or unforced: no change to CFD codes, turbulence closures, injector design or test plans. Effect is P5 confidence only, and real flows cavitate, shock or leave the continuum regime before any singularity matters.
The galactic algorithm results in the release (matrix-multiplication exponent, sub-n log n FFT) do not make CFD, LES or chemistry solvers faster in practice (position e).
Thermochemical Isp ceilings: LOX/CH4 (~380 s vacuum) and LOX/LH2 (~460 s) are fixed by propellant thermochemistry (general). No mathematics raises them; only new propellants or nuclear heating do.

Qualification physics and statistics: bomb tests, duration tests and reliability demonstration (~230 zero-failure tests for 0.99 at 90% confidence) are unchanged unless customers and regulators accept model-based credit.
Launch cadence and tanker count: HLS refueling timing is set by vehicle reliability, pads and flight rate. Better models move it by months at most.
NTP gates: irradiation time to accumulate fluence, HALEU supply, an exhaust-capture test facility, nuclear safety and launch approvals, and appropriations are untouched by AI math.

Solid rocket motors: the constraint is energetics and chemical supply chains and factory capacity (Anduril targets 6,000 tactical motors/yr by end-2026; Raytheon reports motor supply still constrains output), not modeling.

Materials limits: copper-alloy liner temperature, hydrogen attack on fuels and turbine materials, and additive-manufacturing defect scatter are physics and process problems. The DFT ceilings in families 278 and 275 (T1) do not change materials practice.

signposts.event: An independent Comparator run and statement audit of OpenAI's forced Navier–Stokes Lean proof, or of the Buckmaster–Alpöge Euler proofs (next 6-12 months).
signposts.what_it_changes: Moves prop-ns-forced-verified from T3 to T4 with nil engineering change. A gap would remove the precursor for prop-ns-clay-unforced and weaken prop-les-convergence-theory.

signposts.event: Public API access to a research-grade math model (OpenAI or another lab) by mid-2027.
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms S2 timing for every P1 node (certified stability models, automated V&V, gauging, life prediction). Slippage to 2028 or later puts tier-2 nodes on S1 dates.

signposts.event: The first Starship ship-to-ship propellant transfer flies and SpaceX or NASA discloses transferred mass, boil-off and chilldown losses.
signposts.what_it_changes: Unlocks prop-cfm-models and fixes the realistic tanker count for prop-hls-refuel-campaign. Non-disclosure keeps public CFM models data-starved even under S2.

signposts.event: LOXSAT returns on-orbit data and NASA publishes model-vs-flight comparisons for self-pressurization, transfer and gauging.
signposts.what_it_changes: The first public microgravity validation set. It raises prop-cfm-models and prop-mass-gauging confidence and tests whether AI-built models beat the 15-40% errors of current RANS approaches.

signposts.event: An AI-assisted blind prediction of combustion instability (frequency, growth and triggering) on a DLR, Purdue or NASA rig, or AI entries in an AIAA/JANNAF prediction workshop.
signposts.what_it_changes: Success moves prop-flame-response and prop-stability-design-tool toward High in S2; failure holds them at Low or Medium and confirms that data binds.

signposts.event: An AI-derived turbulence closure wins a blind separated-flow or reacting case without retuning.
signposts.what_it_changes: Moves prop-closure-theory from Medium to High in S2 and pulls forward prop-turbopump-tool and the heat-flux inputs to prop-life-twin.

signposts.event: LEAP 71 XRA-2E5 (200 kN) full-duration hot fire, NASA InRoDES vacuum test, Juno in-space RDRE firing.
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms the AI design loop at scale (prop-ai-engine-design-loop) and the RDE flight chain (prop-rde-flight-demo to prop-rde-operational).

signposts.event: FY2027 appropriations and the NASA plan for the ~$110M NTP funding (ground-test facility, reactor or fuel program).
signposts.what_it_changes: Without a funded ground test, the NTP chain stays at Low or Speculative. A program of record moves prop-ntp-ground-test toward Medium in S2/S3.

signposts.event: Mathlib and verified-numerics milestones: formalized finite-volume/Galerkin error estimates, stiff-ODE integrator proofs, floating-point bounds.
signposts.what_it_changes: Gates the certified parts of prop-stiff-chemistry, prop-cfd-auto-vv and prop-verified-engine-software (infra-verified-numerics).

signposts.event: Consecutive Starship flights with full booster and ship engine relight success, including after long coasts.
signposts.what_it_changes: Retires much of the risk on prop-start-transient and the HLS critical path empirically, which would show models following data rather than leading it.
